title: Install Ambassador weekly spotter report (Mar 28–30 2027)
content:
Purpose: quick weekly 'spotter' for installs we shepherded this week — focused on VPC/on-prem handoffs, emergent network blockers, and short-term mitigations. Not a full retro; this is tactical notes + owners to reduce reoccurring friction.

Dates covered: 2027-03-28 through 2027-03-30
Meeting cadence: ad-hoc install triage (daily 09:30 PT), escalation huddles (as-needed)
Attendees: Ethan C (owner), Priya M (field ops), Sofia R (networks), Liam O (install lead), Chen W (SRE oncall)

Summary highlights:
- Two active on-prem installs (Customer: Kestrel Health, Customer: NovaSearch). Both progressed but hit network pathing and cert rotation issues that added ~6–8 hours to day-one handoffs.
- One VPC install (Customer: Logr) rolled back to canary due to MTU mismatch causing gRPC timeouts under batching load. Root cause: site default MTU 1474 + jumbo tuned overlay expected 1500.
- We validated improved preflight checks (new quick-mtu probe) decreased mystery time-to-diagnosis from ~3hrs to ~45m in second install.

Install notes (per customer):
- Kestrel Health (on-prem)
  - Day0: successful node provisioning, kubelet started for all GPU nodes.
  - Blocker: NFS mounts occasionally flapped when backup job (8.10PM) triggered high I/O; caused sidecar volume readiness failures for coordinator pod.
  - Workaround deployed: mark NFS PV with io-priority=low and adjust kubelet grace period for readiness (now 45s -> 120s).
  - Action: Priya to confirm with customer ops that backup schedule will be shifted off peak for next 7 days. Jira: RDW-4123.

- NovaSearch (VPC-connected on-prem)
  - Symptom: intermittent API latency spikes after KV-cache warmup; traced to asymmetric routing through their transit gateway leading to packet reordering.
  - Temp mitigation: route pinning on eBPF sidecar + checksum fallback disabled for affected NICs.
  - Long-term: Sofia + Nova network team to test path MTU and reordering under load in staging; target POC by 2027-04-05. Jira: ENGOPS-987.

- Logr (pure VPC)
  - Symptom: sustained gRPC resets when continuous batching enabled at 400ms; reproducible with infra stress tool.
  - Root cause: MTU mismatch (site 1474 vs expected 1500) causing fragmentation within overlay, gRPC stack not reassembling quickly enough.
  - Fix: added quick-mtu probe to preflight and set autoset-mtu fallback in overlay config; rollback of canary successful.
  - Notes: upgrade to kernel 5.19 on their hosts reduced reassembly latency but not required.

Operational improvements attempted this week:
- Quick-MTU probe: lightweight UDP probe we surface in preflight to detect non-1500 MTU. Deployed to ops-tooling and used in Logr verification; got meaningful reduction in troubleshooting time.
- Cert-rota checklist: observed one customer had expired intermediate cert in their private CA; added explicit intermediate check to installer (now fails preflight with actionable error).
- Install checklist tweak: added an explicit step for 'backups/cron I/O schedule' in pre-install questionnaire to avoid NFS/backup collisions seen with Kestrel.

Outstanding blockers and risk items:
- Persistent: NFS backup + kubelet readiness interaction is brittle on older kernels (<=5.4). Risk level: medium-high for customers with heavy nightly backups. Owner: Priya.
- Network pathing: some transit gateway asymmetries not surfaced by standard traceroute. Risk: medium. Need better active path parity checks. Owner: Sofia.
- HSM/KMS access: one on-prem deploy had HSM endpoint behind a restrictive firewall that blocked key wrapping calls intermittently. Added to runbook but needs cross-org escalation for resolution on customer side. Owner: Liam.

Decisions taken this week:
- Short-term: accept larger kubelet readiness timeout for customers with heavy NFS activity; document in runbook and make configurable per-customer.
- Medium-term: add quick-mtu probe to all preflight templates and surface a clear remediation page in the console when mismatch detected. (Owner: Chen, target 2027-04-07)
- Tooling: small ops CLI change merged to allow rerunning installer preflight without re-creating resources (PR: ops#278).

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Priya M: Confirm Kestrel backup schedule shift and close RDW-4123 by 2027-04-01.
- Sofia R: Run 'path parity' POC with Nova network team; share findings 2027-04-05.
- Chen W: Implement console remediation copy for MTU mismatch + wire quick-mtu to console alert UI by 2027-04-07.
- Liam O: Open escalation to customer security team for HSM firewall rules and track resolution; target 2027-04-04.

Notes to field engineers / playbook updates:
- If encountering flaky NFS mounts during Day0, increase kubelet pod-infra grace and check for concurrent backup I/O; ask customer to pause cron jobs for initial 48 hours when possible.
- Run quick-mtu probe as first post-preflight network test. If mismatch, surface 'suggested remediation' with exact iptables / network team steps.

Misc:
- Time to successful first inference (end-to-end) improved from median 11h -> 9.2h on installs using the new checklist (sample n=6). We should track this metric as a KPI for install improvements.
- Customer delight note: Kestrel engineer called out the 'installer verbosity' improvements in logs as "immediately helpful" — small UX wins matter.

Open questions:
- Do we want to make quick-mtu probe strict (fail preflight) or advisory with suggested remediation? Recommend advisory first, then strict after one release cycle.
- Should we standardize a 'backup blackout window' doc for customers during first-week handoffs? (proposal: 48h by default)

Appendix: quick links
- Handoff checklist (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Ambassador+Handoff+Checklist
- Jira: RDW-4123 (Kestrel NFS issue), ENGOPS-987 (Nova path parity)
- Ops PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/278

If anything missing or if you want a deeper retro on a specific install, ping me and I'll schedule a short post-mortem.

-- Ethan
short_summary: Weekly 'spotter' for three installs: Kestrel (on-prem) NFS I/O flaps; Nova (VPC-onprem) asymmetric routing; Logr (VPC) MTU-induced gRPC resets. Quick-mtu probe and checklist tweaks reduced time-to-diagnosis. Action items assigned.
